segments.expected: "The tear was here," said Vane. He put his finger on a place on the moor's top, a mile north of the hut, where three gills began. "On the Saturday, at four. I'd six on the Sag and two up here; we had it shut by eleven. Four came off it first." He moved the finger. "Three went down this gill. Together. Slow. I've had a lad on the Edge with a glass every day since, and they've gone a little way each day, down, and stopped, and gone on. Yesterday they were here." He tapped a place where the gill came out of the moor's edge into the head of a narrow wooded valley. "This morning they were here."

segments.expected: It was not that she was surprised. She had told Jude that she was not to be trusted, and she had meant it, and she had been right. It was that she had let herself want a thing on a moor, for an hour, with her whole body, for the first time since a hill in the autumn. The wanting had nowhere to go, and went down through her into the frozen peat like a still door with nothing under it.
